sources.claim: Streets, crosswalks, signal locations, Line 2 schedule, building footprints and business presence for Bloor St W, Bathurst–Spadina
Adult PRESTO fare CAD 3.30; Fair Pass CAD 2.10 (citywide rule)
Business presence and names; no sales, staffing or hours
2025 Bloor counter west of Huron: 3,524 passages/day; context, not a removal effect

assumptions.note: People, home assignments, routines, budgets and preferences are invented test inputs, shared by both policies.
Choice score = preference − cost × cost sensitivity × cost weight − total minutes / 30 × time sensitivity − shared-with-cars km × safety sensitivity × discomfort, plus fixed seeded variation.
Minutes beyond the 619 m section are fixed per option and do not change with either policy.
Parking and driving costs per trip are illustrative.
Purchase amounts are illustrative; OSM supplies presence only.
A focal shop closes at 18:00 the next period if this sample’s receipts fall below its stated floor; this is not a closure or sales model.
Scales every person’s response to money cost.

assumptions.unit: utility per km shared with cars
assumptions.note: How much riding in a car lane lowers a cyclist’s choice score, before personal safety sensitivity. No observed Toronto removal response.
Off gives the zero-retail-response case: shops keep their hours whatever the receipts.

limitations: Synthetic people, routines, budgets, baskets and preferences: a mechanism demonstration, not a Toronto forecast.
Choices come from a stated synthetic score (or a bounded external provider); no Toronto fare elasticity or removal response is estimated.
Only foreground agents move; background traffic is observed entry flow, so agents do not congest each other.
Cyclists in car lanes move at bike speed; removal changes exposure distance and comfort, not travel time, injuries or speed.
Shop hours respond to a synthetic receipts floor; OSM supplies business presence only.
Minutes beyond the 619 m section are fixed per option and policy-invariant.
